newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's sees turnover up 3.0 pct/1997.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's sees turnover up 3.0 pct/1997.

text.p: Morocco's sugar company Cosumar, which controls 80 percent of the local market, forecast growth of 3.0 percent in 1997 compared with an estimated 2.6 percent this year, due mainly to positive agricultural expectations.
Cosumar showed in its half-year results that turnover dropped slightly to 1.6 billion dirhams ($184 million) from January to June 1996 after 1.7 billion dirhams in the same period in 1995.
Noureddine Benmakhlouf, managing director of Cosumar, told Reuters the decline was largely due to "the bad weather which hit the sugar crop in early 1996."
An estimated 40,000 hectares (100,000 acres) of sugar beet and cane were damaged by floods in several areas of the country.

Compagnie Sucriere Marocaine (Cosumar), which was set up in 1929 in Casablanca, operates a fully integrated sugar refinery. It also runs two mills and processes raw sugar either produced by local mills or imported.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, holds more than 66 percent of Cosumar's capital of 419.1 million dirhams.
The firm, which suffers from Morocco's cyclical droughts, saw its output down to 595,256 tonnes of sugar in 1995 from 626,986 tonnes in the previous year.
Turnover also fell 5.6 percent to 3.15 billion dirhams in 1995 compared with 1994.
"Cosumar is likely to suffer from new competitors and lose its monopoly over the refined sugar market in future," one analyst at Upline Securities said.
But Cosumar officials remain confident, arguing that the company has already drawn up a long term strategy to face the impact of sugar liberalisation.

"We prepared ourselves years before the government took the decision to liberalise the commodity market...What we need is a three-year transition period to adapt to the new environment," Benmakhlouf said.

In 1993, Cosumar completed its vertical integration with the purchase of two sugar plants in the rich farming areas of Doukkala on the Atlantic coast. But it is also still interested in 10 others on the list for privatisation by end 1998.
Cosumar, which refuses to release details of its imports in the last three months, is expected to import nearly half of the 500,000 tonnes of raw sugar neeeded for domestic consumption of 1996.
Sugar consumption among Morocco's 27 million population has reached 33 kg per head, one of the world's highest figures.
